- **[GUI Control Scope]** No page and no graphical control surface: the terminal fleet console (matrix#v2-14) is the one view beyond `viola list`, and what it shows is the route entry «Fleet console view»'s to name.

- **[Deferred] Deferred to specialists and later versions:** auth generally (security, v1.x); the test framework, fake-agent harness and `viola verify` probe design (tests); logging and observability (obs); self-update, signing and a marketplace entry (later version).
**GUI contracts.** None: viola has no web or graphical surface; the terminal fleet console's contracts (matrix#v2-14) are owed by the route entry «Console scaffold».

- **Scale path.**
  - v1 is personal and Linux only (first live on the Linux dev host, by the founder's ruling R-L1; CI-tested on `ubuntu-latest` against the fake agent; the Windows and macOS code recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`).
  - v1.x adds public distribution (dist 0.33.0 releases, signing, a marketplace entry, self_update 1.3.0).

- Code-graph planes (`scripts/code-graph.py`, one DuckDB per language plane under `.andromeda/cache/{plane}/`):
  - **rust:** the root workspace through rust-analyzer SCIP. It indexes every member (`viola`, `viola-core`, `viola-pty`, `viola-channel`, `viola-agent-claude`, `viola-state`, `viola-mcp`, `viola-e2e`). `fuzz/`, a separate workspace, is outside it.
  - **ts:** none: the tree tracks no `tsconfig.json`, so `scripts/code-graph.py` detects no ts plane.

- **Approach:** none for v1 (as of 2026-09-23). The only principal is the local OS user.
  - Reason: Project Intent and Established Decisions (Personal v1) describe a single-user local tool with "no accounts, no hosting".
  - Access control therefore depends entirely on OS-level isolation: who can connect to each IPC endpoint and who can read or write `~/.viola/`. Cross-cutting Patterns (Local endpoint trust boundary) sets the target principal as "every process of the same OS user and no other".
  - The enforcement mechanism for that boundary is this specialist's: Authentication & Authorization sets it, enforced on Linux, the one target.

No web surface: viola renders no page. The keyboard-driven terminal fleet console tiled on Hyprland (matrix#v2-14) takes its own surface section at the route entry «Console scaffold».

- **Line form (stderr):** `unable  <name>  <reason>  <detail>`, fields separated by two spaces. `viola send` pads `unable` into the mirror's word column after `[/ ]`. The fixed-message exceptions are the exit-1 start refusals of `viola run` (`unable: <name> is already live` and its sibling causes, listed in design-system cli pattern 2), the exit-1 refusals of `viola revive` (the same collision pair, and its own five pairs under Output structure — `viola revive`; under `--json` its `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` document in place of the pair) and `viola verify`'s exit-1 refusals, each an `unable: <text>` line and its own `hint:` line with no name, path or pid: `the claude CLI was not found` / `install Claude Code or put it on PATH`; `the CLI version could not be read` / `run claude --version to check the install`; `a recorded fixture is not clean: <file> <code>` (a screen fixture: `<file> row <n>[ seam] <code>`; codes `home-path` · `absolute-path` · `username` · `email`; it names the fixture file and the check, never the content) / `record with a viola home under your user home`; `verify was stopped before it finished` / `run viola verify again to stamp this CLI` (a run stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM, stdout empty); `the viola home is not private to you` / `the viola home must be readable only by you; viola does not change its permissions` (the home pair: its strict-modes check refuses the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` or `plugin/` before its log opens, or refuses the stamps write; stdout empty, no step line, no summary); plus run's pinned-copy refusal; and the home-tree refusal of the `viola run` and `viola revive` starts, checked before the wrapper log opens: the home pair for the home, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/` or the pinned copy's folders and file, `revive`'s instance pair for the instance's state files, no log opened, no line, no child; and the socket-directory refusal of the `viola run` and `viola revive` starts, exit 1, made before any snapshot, child or bind, stdout empty and the directory left as found: `unable: the socket directory for <name> cannot be trusted` / `hint: viola's socket directory must be a directory you own, readable only by you; viola does not change its permissions` (under `revive --json` its document, Output structure — `viola revive`); and `viola list`'s exit-21 strict-modes refusal of the whole board (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list; the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer, the operator's answer superseded 2026-10-13), stdout empty: `unable: the viola home is not private to you` / `hint: the viola home must be readable only by you; viola does not change its permissions` for the home or `instances/`, and `unable: <name>'s state files can be written by another user` / `hint: viola will not read them; make the viola home and its files owner-only` (`revive`'s pair) for one instance; and `viola plugin install`'s exit-21 strict-modes refusal, stdout empty, the same home pair for the home or a `marketplace/` tree dir, nothing created and no log opened; and the exit-21 strict-modes refusal of the frame verbs `viola send` (after its text read), `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link` and `unlink` (for these two `<name>` is the driven instance), made before any role file or log opens, stdout empty: `revive`'s instance pair (`unable: <name>'s state files can be written by another user` / `hint: viola will not read them; make the viola home and its files owner-only`), no line written to any log and the directory's mode left as found; under `--json` `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` with stderr empty. A failed or panicked `cli` verb (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `list`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `verify`, `revive --list`, `plugin install`, `link`, `unlink`; a `revive` start stays outside it) prints exactly `error: internal error` once, from the one catch site, with no hint, and with `--json` among the arguments before a `--` prints `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout in its place with stderr empty (for `wait` / `last` exit 1 also covers a refusal reply, an unparseable reply or any other channel error; for `link` / `unlink` a refusal reply or an `ok` of another shape; for `list` an `instances/` that cannot be listed and a log start that fails, while a per-instance read error gives no row).

- **Hint line:** directly under each refusal, `hint: <one plain instruction>`, keyed by reason (or by reason · detail). Exit 21 and exit 1 each have several causes, and every cause gets its own hint, so an agent can tell the causes apart from the last stderr line (design-system cli pattern 2). The exit-1 start refusal `unable: <name> is already live` takes `hint: viola list`. `wait`, `last`, `link` and `unlink`'s exit 21 `unable  <name>  instance-unreachable` (for `link` / `unlink`, `<name>` is the driven instance) takes `hint: <name> is not running; viola list shows the live instances` when the instance is not running (`viola send`'s exit 21 keeps its `[/ ] unable` mirror with the same hint). A frame verb's exit 21 on a name with no directory at its instance path takes `hint: <name> is not a wrapped session; only sessions started with viola run take commands`, and with its wrapper lost while the call is open `hint: <name>'s wrapper went away during the call; viola list shows whether it is still running`, each the last stderr line in plain ASCII. A frame verb (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`) whose server check finds that the process on the endpoint is not the recorded wrapper, or cannot make the check, writes no frame and exits 21 with the same `unable  <name>  instance-unreachable` line (`send` in its `[/ ] unable` mirror) and `hint: the process on <name>'s endpoint is not its recorded wrapper; it was not contacted` as the last stderr line; under `--json` it prints the exit-21 document `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"server-verify-failed"}` with stderr empty. A frame verb meeting a refused socket directory writes no frame and exits 21 with the same `unable  <name>  instance-unreachable` line (`send` in its `[/ ] unable` mirror) and `hint: viola's socket directory must be a directory you own, readable only by you; viola does not change its permissions` as the last stderr line; under `--json` it prints the exit-21 document `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"socket-dir-refused"}` with stderr empty. There is no hint for the `unknown` refusal, whose detail is a code word or nothing, for `wrapper fault` or for `internal error`. A hint never quotes the sent text or any upstream text, and never names a path or a pid.

- **Flat verbs:** one lower-case word each (`plugin install` is the one two-word verb). There is no nested noun hierarchy, no interactive prompt and no pager in a verb; the terminal fleet console (matrix#v2-14) is no verb's output, and its own surface is owed by the route entry «Console scaffold».

- **Shared vocabulary:**
  - The six captions, words and slot order are fixed, and the terminal fleet console (matrix#v2-14) reuses them.
  - The readback vocabulary is `open`, `read back`, `unable`, `unconfirmable`. The CLI brackets the box.
  - ` - ` separates inside a CLI field, and an arrow is `->`. There is no CLI inbound `<-` form.
  - Amber means `DIALOG` and nothing else. `stale` is SGR dim in the terminal.
  - The CLI is where every action lives.

- Command body: `scripts/agent-run.sh run [--unit|--integration|--e2e|--mutants|--coverage|--perf|--fuzz-replay|--all] [--filter <nextest-filterset>] [--file <path>]... [--package <member>] [--local-live]`. `--file` (repeatable) needs `--mutants` (clap `requires`): it scopes the mutation run to those sources, the inner fix-loop (step 4). `--package` also needs `--mutants`: it mutates one whole member, the boundary tier's form (step 4 Package). `--coverage`, `--fuzz-replay` and `--mutants` never join the default selection. With no selector and no `--local-live` the default is `--all`, which runs steps 1 and 2 in order (`--local-live` passed alone is a selection of its own and runs neither step); step 4 runs only under `--mutants`:
  1. Unit + integration: `cargo nextest run --workspace --features viola/fake-agent --profile ci -E '<layer filterset>'`, then `cargo test --workspace --doc`, both with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<workspace root>/target/harness` (boot step 1). JUnit is still read from `<workspace root>/target/nextest/ci/junit.xml`: nextest's store is workspace-root-relative whatever the target dir (measured 2026-09-24). The layer filtersets are:
     - unit: `kind(lib) | kind(bin)`
     - integration: `kind(test) & !binary(/^(path[0-9]*|tui|mcp|cross|chaos|contract)_/)`, the complement of step 2's layer, so a test binary reports in exactly one of the two. A `binary()` regex that matches no binary is a nextest filterset parse error, not an empty set (as measured on cargo-nextest 0.9.146 on the Linux dev host at chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs: a scratch crate, exit 94 "operator didn't match any binary names"; first measured on 0.9.133, 2026-09-24); the regex matches the root `chaos_`, `contract_`, `cross_`, `tui_` and `path<N>_` binaries, so both layers parse in this workspace, and the harness's own throwaway-workspace cases plant one `path_` binary before an integration run.
  2. Fake-agent E2E: `cargo nextest run --workspace --features viola/fake-agent --profile ci -E 'binary(/^(path[0-9]*|tui|mcp|cross|chaos|contract)_/)'`, suite `nextest-e2e`, run third after step 1's two nextest runs (`run --e2e`; in the default and `--all`), through the same nextest shape and target dir, a `--filter` intersecting it. `[0-9]*` after `path` admits the numbered Path binaries (`path1_run_start`, `path6_budget_harness`), which the written `^(path|…)_` did not select (as measured at chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs: 18 binaries, and `run --integration` ran `path1`). 20 binaries / 157 tests at that chunk's end. `run --e2e` alone runs no doctest (doctest stays with step 1 and `--coverage`); the run-archive list is unchanged (unit, integration and coverage JUnit). Every nextest test uses one boot model:
     - No test shells out to `agent-run` / `viola-harness`, so there is never a nested `cargo run` inside nextest.
     - Root `tests/` suites use the rstest chain `home → fake_agent_path → stamped_home → booted_wrapper`.
     - `crates/viola-e2e` scenarios use one of two boot models, chosen by the scenario's §6 Cleanup line:
       - Cleanup "harness `cleanup`" (Paths 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, E3): `viola_e2e::harness::session::harness_session(test, label, opts) -> HarnessSession`, a plain function and drop guard (`viola-e2e` carries no `[dev-dependencies]`, so never an rstest fixture), landed at chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs. It calls the same library code as the `boot` / `cleanup` commands (`viola_e2e::harness::{boot, cleanup}`) with `stamp: !opts.unstamped` (`SessionOptions::unstamped`, default false, so the default session is stamped — the in-test form of `boot --unstamped`, chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers, whose Path 7 MCP leg boots the default `overseer` + `builder` pair unstamped, `SessionOptions { unstamped: true, ..SessionOptions::default() }`), and the library `boot` spawns the `supervise` process from the given binary dir, so `cleanup`'s pid + start-time proof stays exact (fork 2 of that chunk, `inputs#I1`). `SessionOptions` defaults to `overseer` + `builder`, no `--statusline-echo`, `--agents-mode recorded`, stamped (`unstamped` false); the guard exposes `home()`, `instance_dir(name)`, `bin_dir()`, `session()`, `workspace()` and `cleanup(self)`, panics with the boot document unless ready, and never shells out to `agent-run`. Its `Drop` runs `cleanup` (the home kept) unless `cleanup(self)` ran, then removes the home's parent unless `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1`, or `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1` while the test is panicking. `harness_session` always skips boot step 1, so no `cargo build` runs inside nextest. It passes `viola_e2e::harness::boot` the binary dir found from the test executable's own target dir, never a literal `target/<profile>`, and boot step 3 copies the fake agent from that same dir. This is the same binary-dir parameter `--perf` uses (§10). As a result, the scenarios spawn the instrumented `viola` / `viola-fake-agent` under `--coverage`, and the plain debug binaries otherwise.
       - Cleanup "TempDir drop" or a test-owned outer PTY (Paths 1, 5, E1, E2, E5): the chain `home → fake_agent_path → stamped_home → booted_wrapper` from `viola_e2e::fixtures`. Root `tests/support/` cannot be imported by another package, and the root package must not dev-depend on the tokio-based `viola-e2e`, so the chain exists twice (the sync root copy and the `viola-e2e` copy) against one contract. In both copies `stamped_home` runs `viola verify` against the fake agent. Today only the sync root copy exists (`tests/support/home.rs`; homes under `target/e2e-home/viola-test-*`). The `viola_e2e::fixtures` copy lands with its first consumer among these scenarios; Path 1's flow is not one, landing on the root chain as `tests/path1_run_start.rs` (fork 1 of chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs, `inputs#I1`). The root `stamped_home` runs `viola --home <h> verify -- <fake agent> --cli-version 2.1.287 --fixtures <root>/fixtures/claude` (the committed recorded set; `2.1.287` is the root chain's one literal, `tests/support/fake.rs` `RECORDED_CLI_VERSION`), and `stamped` is true only on exit 0 and a last line `stamped 2.1.287  <n> pass  0 fail`; anything else panics with the exit and match codes. `StampedHome::unstamped(TestHome)` (`stamped:false`, writes nothing) serves the tests that assert the unverified path. `booted_wrapper` drives the wrapper through a test-owned outer PTY (`tests/support/outer_pty.rs`; `Wrapper::boot/send/stop` in `tests/support/home.rs`, and `tests/run_cli.rs::run_viola`) and waits for `process-start` lines for `self` and `claude-child` and a fake-agent `start` receipt, each newer than the boot (a `gone` name's files are reused) — the receipt means its terminal is raw, so no key sent after it is swallowed — then for the snapshot (`pid`, `started_at`, `child_pid`) and a heartbeat under 5 s, bounded at 7 s — `WITHIN` in `tests/support/watch.rs`, shared by the root waits on a child (`Instant::now() + WITHIN` reads 31 sites in 23 files under `tests/` (`grep -rn 'Instant::now() + WITHIN' tests/ | wc -l` and `grep -rln 'Instant::now() + WITHIN' tests/ | wc -l`), as measured at chunk 2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci's wrap on the Linux dev host; architecture §Occupied Resources → Filesystem states the count's rule) and strictly below the nextest `mutants` profile's 10 s kill, so a stuck wait fails the test itself. `Wrapper::boot` always passes `--cli-version 2.1.287` (`--fixtures` stays a per-test extra). `Wrapper::stop` / `stop_keep` wait for the wrapper's exit and then, when the snapshot recorded an `endpoint`, for that endpoint to be unconnectable (`wait_endpoint_gone`; `unconnectable` is the harness `endpoint_gone` rule — a connect to the path is refused or the path is absent, what `holder_gone` reads). The kill path (`Wrapper::kill`, used by `tests/chaos_revive.rs`) kills the wrapper the test booted, waits for its exit, then for the child it recorded to be gone by pid and start time, then on `holder_gone` in place of `wait_endpoint_gone`: a connect to the path is refused or the path is absent. A killed wrapper removes nothing, so on Unix its socket file stays (the next bind takes over a leftover socket file) and a wait on the file being absent never ends after a kill (as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive; the kill-and-revive case green on a run of the retired three-OS matrix). The stop path keeps the `unconnectable` rule. An exit code is not the endpoint gone. Each wait notes what it polls (codes, counts and booleans, read in the predicate's own short-circuit order) to `<temp dir>/viola-root-watch/<test>.<label>.report`, one line per change, kept on a failure or a runner kill and removed on a pass. The wait is exit-aware: when `child.try_wait()` reports that the wrapper exited first, it fails at once (`wrapper <name> exited before ready`) instead of waiting out the bound. The bound stays below cargo-mutants' 20 s auto-timeout floor, so a mutant that stops the wrapper from getting ready grades as caught, not Timeout. Harness `boot` keeps its 20 s per-instance bound.
     - In §6, a step written `agent-run boot --session <id> <flags>` means `harness_session` with those flags. A Cleanup written `agent-run cleanup --session <id>` means harness `cleanup` as defined below. The `<id>` there (`p2`, `p7`) is only a readable label. The real session id always follows the `<test name>-<label>-<pid>` rule below, so neither parallel tests nor two sessions opened by one test (Path 7) share a session.
     - "Harness `cleanup`" means the test calls `session.cleanup()` at the end and asserts the report: no field `false` (an interim `null` field is allowed), same shape as the `cleanup` command. `Drop` is only a best-effort fallback for panicking tests.
     - The session id is `<test name>-<label>-<pid>`, where `<label>` is the §6 `--session` label (`p2`, `p7`, `p7-stamped`) or `main` when the step gives none. The loss lies between the ConPTY input-pipe write and that test child's read; **where inside that span, and why, is not established** — an overseer read of microsoft/terminal's current source (relayed at the wrap, not verified here) found no input-buffer flush on the resize path and no reported resize input loss, so this is not recorded as a ConPTY defect. **The product window — open and unmeasured for `claude`:** viola forwards resizes and keys as they come and never holds, queues or reorders a human key behind a resize (a11y-plan §1), so nothing in viola closes this window. Whether the real `claude` (Node/libuv, reading with `ReadConsoleInputW`) loses a key typed right after a resize in `viola run` is **unmeasured**; the rate above is the Rust test child's. body: **"Strip-bay handoff, read back."** The direction the CLI carries, and the terminal fleet console (matrix#v2-14) inherits, is an air-traffic-control tower strip bay after dark. Buff paper strips sit in anthracite holder boots on ruled aluminium racks, and every session keeps its slot for life. The only warm light is the one amber arrival holder cocked out of line when a session needs you. The voice is standard phraseology: short fixed words (`open`, `RB`, `unable`, `human-typing`, `budget-paused`), no filler, no guessing. Nothing announces success before it is confirmed: a send stays `open` until the matching `prompt-submitted` reads it back (for `/clear`, until its new-session post-condition does; for `/compact` on a verified CLI, until its same-session compact post-condition does, and on an unverified CLI `/compact` stays `unconfirmable`). Missing readings print `unknown`, and old information carries its age (`read 4m ago`, `expired`). It is explicitly NOT a monitoring dashboard: no status dots, toasts, graphs, spinners or glow.

STATUS `idle` / `busy` on a row the read joins, else `unknown`; a failed read prints the board as with no `claude`; and a failed strict-modes check refuses the whole board with exit 21, or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`), the `viola send` readback mirror (an unusable `viola send` and an oversize `viola answer` instead exit 2 with their fixed stderr line, `UNUSABLE_TEXT` / `UNUSABLE_RESPONSE`, whatever `--json` says, and no document; a failed `cli` verb's `error: internal error`, exit 1, is with `--json` among the arguments before a `--` the document `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout with stderr empty, while `run`, `revive`'s start, `mcp` and `hook` stay silent at the catch site), phraseology verb output (`viola plugin install`: four plain-ASCII stdout lines in one write, no SGR, `viola@viola  written  <dir>` / `run these to add it to Claude Code:` / `  claude plugin marketplace add <dir>` / `  claude plugin install viola@viola`, `<dir>` quoted only where the host's shell would split it; `viola revive <name> --list` prints one static line per logged session; under `--json` both arms print one stdout document: `--list`'s `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[…]}}`, every refusal of the start it shares with `run`, `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` with exit 1, no hint and stderr empty, `<code>` one of `strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing` · `stale-heartbeat` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `socket-dir-refused` · `internal-error`;
